findings.claim: REFEREE bus finding (2026-09-01, to BP2-METER): the live orchestrator ledger read status=complete while 4 legs were running - rails.py to_dict mapped open->complete. Actioned as T4-class: to_dict now reports the actual status; a live run reads 'open'; charge/settle persist via _persist() (stays open); only an explicit close() finalises to 'complete'; blocked unchanged.
findings.resolution: fixed on branch bp2/meter; the LIVE orchestrator runs the main-tree rails.py and is unaffected until a human merges.

findings.claim: Adversarial verify (dim 1, MAJOR): measure_transcript_tokens crashed on a JSON-valid record with a non-integer usage value (int() guarded only by except OSError) - violated 'a torn transcript never crashes'.
findings.resolution: fixed - _as_int coerces defensively (bad field -> 0 for that field, never fatal).

findings.claim: Adversarial verify (dim 1, MINOR): an empty/field-absent usage dict returned a MEASURED (0,0) instead of UNKNOWN - a default masquerading as measured, violating 'absent token renders UNKNOWN, never 0'.
findings.resolution: fixed - a record counts as measured only when it genuinely carries a primary token field.

findings.claim: Adversarial verify (dim 4, MINOR): settling the same leg twice opened a second turn, contradicting 'turns are never double-charged' (latent; the orchestrator settles once per done-transition).
findings.resolution: fixed - a re-settle updates the existing entry in place, never opens a turn.

findings.claim: Adversarial verify (dim 4, MINOR): orchestrate.ps1 omitted --date, so a wave crossing midnight would look under runs/<D+1>/ and lose the ledger opened on <D>; settle's exit-7-only check missed the resulting exit-2 (tokens silently dropped).
findings.anchor: harness/orchestrate.ps1 $script:RailsDate pinned at open, threaded through open/charge/settle; Rails-Settle surfaces any non-zero exit
findings.resolution: fixed - one ledger date for the whole run; a settle that cannot record is surfaced loudly, never silent.
